title: Search Backend
observations: Architecture reviewer caught CRITICAL FINDING-1 (hostKind contract bug) in Phase 2 critique before build. Without this, every conversation result would be silently dropped by frontend parser. Silent-data-loss bug prevented by two-phase gate.
TDD red phase (12 test cases, 581 lines) covered all 5 ACs exhaustively. Zero surprise edge cases in code review. Pattern matches AA1, AA3, AB2, AB3 (CC-010 confirmed X5).

Code review found 3 blocking contract violations (B-1: null appetite, B-2: null layer/kind, B-3: N+1 query loop) all stemming from builder not consulting architecture plan sections 5-6. Builder not reading response mapping sections (6.1-6.3).

Builder's rework fixed N+1 loop with batch query approach superior to plan's sub-selects: 3 total queries, explicit application-layer joining, more scalable. Contract violation caught in review, fix improved on plan.
Rework cost 13% (1h of 7.5h total) acceptable for backend route with multiple contract boundaries. Clean critique→code→rework→re-review handoff. All findings correctly applied.
cost_signals: Builder did not read response mapping section (6.1-6.3) of architecture plan before implementation; all contract violations (B-1, B-2, B-3) stemmed from this.
Self-review gate before code review would catch contract mismatches 20 minutes instead of 1+ hour.
Two-phase critique+code-review gate as safety net: architecture critic caught FINDING-1 (silent-data-loss), code reviewer caught B-1/B-2/B-3 (response shape). Neither alone sufficient.
compound_candidates: CC-010: TDD red phase prevents silent bugs (confirmed X5: AA1, AA3, AB2, AB3, AD3, AD7)
CC-009: Critique effectiveness when plan detail level high (confirmed X4: AA1, AA3, AB3, AD7 — detailed sections enable cross-checking)
CC-001: Code review gates catch contract violations from arch→build handoff (confirmed X3: AB2 design-handoff, AD7 response-shape, prior examples)
CC-008: Batch query pattern superior to sub-selects at small scale (new observation: batch+app-join more readable and scalable than correlated sub-selects)
